title: Fast-fail routing shim and tracelet telemetry for customer 5xx surges
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden increases in 5xx responses and client-observed timeouts during a high-traffic window (2026-03-09 07:00-09:30 UTC). Root cause appears to be a short-lived interaction between our upstream edge router backpressure heuristic and the new batch coalescer: under a burst pattern, requests were queued past the kernel-level socket deadlines and then retried by SDKs leading to amplification.

Observed behavior:
- Spike in backend error rate (5xx) correlated with elevated connection queuing durations on edge proxies.
- Long tail of client timeouts even after service recovered due to in-flight request retries and delayed failure propagation.
- Customers with heavy streaming workloads saw higher error surface.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled a narrow routing policy change at 2026-03-09 09:40 UTC to reduce max inflight per-tenant on the edge (manual rollback ready).
- Issued customer comms summarizing impact and temporary controls; suggested SDK retry-reduce patch for affected customers.

Proposed permanent fix (this ticket):
1) Implement a fast-fail routing shim on the edge which short-circuits requests when per-tenant queueing exceeds safe thresholds to avoid durability of sockets in the slow path. Fast-fail returns structured 429/503 with consistent retry-after when appropriate.
2) Emit a lightweight "tracelet" telemetry event per request at edge + runtime entry points with fields: request_id, tenant_id_hash, queue_ms, kernel_wait_ms, batch_id, model_variant. These must be high-cardinality-safe (hashed IDs) and shardable.
3) Add an adaptive client-facing header that surfaces a deterministic retry token for idempotency (used for safe dedup in SDKs and edge).

Trade-offs:
- Fast-fail increases client-visible failures briefly but prevents amplification and accelerates recovery; we will combine with clear retry semantics to limit customer retries.
- Tracelet telemetry adds volume to our ingest; will sample 10% by default and 100% for error paths.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for shim logic and header propagation.
- Integration test in staging with synthetic tenant burst generator (see infra perf test: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/tenant-burst-sim).
- Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in hosted region us-west-2 with rapid kill switch. Metrics to watch: 5xx rate (v2), queue_ms p95/p99, retry token collisions, customer error reports.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR and feature-flag behind edge.fast_fail_shim (ENG-100812-fastfail-shim).
- Deploy edge binaries to staging. Run 24h soak.
- Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows.
- Post-deploy: monitor escalation channel and incident dashboard for 12h.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Fast-Fail+Shim+and+Tracelets
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2387
- Staging perf test: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/tenant-burst-sim

Open questions:
- Exact sampling ratio for tracelets to balance observability vs cost (proposal: 10% baseline, 100% on 5xx and timeout).
- Compatibility with Dedicated/private deployments where customers may have different retry policies; need config gating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fast-fail shim returns deterministic failure codes when thresholds hit and reduces 5xx amplification by >=60% in synthetic bursts.
- Tracelet events appear in ES/dataset with tenant hash and queue_ms for >=90% of error traces in canary.
- SDKs accept retry token and dedupe behavior validated in integration tests.
